Dominance

One ratio that explains the market

Bitcoin's share of total crypto market cap is the market's risk gauge. When it rises, money is hiding in the biggest asset. When it falls, money is reaching for everything else.

The dominance cycle

The pattern has repeated three times. Early in a cycle Bitcoin leads: it is the most liquid, the first asset institutions buy, and the one with a narrative (halving, ETFs) that does not depend on anything shipping. Dominance rises. Then Bitcoin stalls, capital rotates to Ethereum, and from Ethereum to the large alternative platforms, and from those to the small caps and memecoins. Dominance falls steeply — from 70% to 40% in the first half of 2021 — and the fall is itself the signal that the cycle is maturing. In the bust, everything falls but Bitcoin falls least, and dominance climbs back.

Reading an altseason

The common definition is that 75% of the top 50 coins outperform Bitcoin over 90 days. By that measure full altseasons are rare — a few months in 2017–18, a few in 2021 — and most of the time Bitcoin wins. The practical implication is uncomfortable for altcoin holders: over any full cycle, the median altcoin has underperformed Bitcoin badly, and the ones that outperformed were a small, hard-to-predict set. The 2024–25 cycle was unusual in that dominance kept rising through the bull market, because ETF money could only buy Bitcoin.

The Ethereum ratio

ETH/BTC is the second-most-watched ratio. It peaked near 0.15 in 2017 and 0.085 in 2021, and spent 2024–25 below 0.04, its lowest in years, as capital flowed to Bitcoin ETFs and to Solana. Whether this reflects a permanent change in Ethereum's standing or a cyclical low is a live debate; the ratio has made fools of confident forecasters in both directions.

Stablecoins as a share

Stablecoin dominance is the inverse signal: it rises when people sell into cash and wait. Its 2022 peak of about 17% marked the bottom of that bear market within a few weeks. Watching the three series together — Bitcoin, Ethereum, stablecoins — is as good a one-chart summary of market regime as exists.
